title: Elastic throughput corridors and tenant-aware slowpath fallback for dedicated fleets
creator: Priya Patel
description: Design and implement 'elastic throughput corridors' for dedicated GPU fleets: a per-tenant windowed reservation (min guarantee) and a bounded burst ceiling (soft max) that work together with a tenant-aware slowpath fallback. The feature set includes: (1) per-tenant corridor parameters (min, soft_max, hard_max, window_ms), (2) a fastpath for small/latency-sensitive requests that bypasses slow queues when tokens available, (3) a slowpath queue with progressive priority decay and probabilistic shedding when headroom is exhausted, and (4) autoscaler hinting signals derived from corridor saturation metrics (burst_rate, sustained_util, queue_depth_percentile) to drive scale-up decisions. Goals: preserve P95 latency for latency-sensitive tenants, bound worst-case throughput for tenants to avoid noisy-neighbor failures, and provide clear observability and safe degradation modes for Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable per-tenant corridor parameters visible in Console and via API
Fastpath preserves P95 latency within SLO for small requests under normal load
Slowpath queue depth stays bounded under synthetic overload tests and shedding keeps fleet stable
Autoscaler accepts corridor-derived hints and performs conservative scale-up in canary test
E2E test harness with tenant-mix replay shows no cross-tenant throughput collapse in 99% of runs
comments: 2025-07-15 - Kickoff: reviewed high-level design with PM and runtime leads. Agreed on token-window model vs absolute reservation to maximize utilization. Action: Priya to produce sequence diagrams and capacity math.

2025-07-18 - Design decision: use a windowed leaky-bucket plus fastpath token pool sized by p50 request size to favor latency-sensitive traffic. Rationale: keeps burstability for small requests while protecting long-running heavy requests.

2025-07-22 - Trade-off note: probabilistic shedding (early-drop with rate proportional to overload) chosen over pure LIFO eviction to avoid starvation of smaller tenants. Potential downside: slightly non-deterministic error surface for customers; PM asked for explicit rollback flag.

2025-07-27 - Implementation update: initial queue adapter and corridor evaluator merged to branch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234. Performance smoke tests attached to PR show end-to-end P95 degradation under controlled overload < 10% for fastpath TLs.

2025-07-30 - Observability: added corridor saturation metrics (corridor_util_pct, burst_consumed, slowpath_drop_rate) to dogfood dashboard. Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Elastic+Throughput+Corridors

2025-08-02 - Blocker discovered: race between autoscaler hint emission and token reclamation on preempted requests can cause transient overcommit. Mitigation: add conservative cooldown window for hint emission (implemented as autotuner parameter). Follow-up: ENG-246811 to harden reclamation path.
implementation_notes: Runtime: corridor evaluator runs at ingress and annotates request with admission verdict (fastpath|enqueued|dropped)
Queue: slowpath uses segmented queues per-tenant with decay-based priority and a per-tenant soft-shrink policy to reclaim headroom under sustained overload
Shedding: early probabilistic drops when soft_max exceeded; hard_max triggers deterministic reject with descriptive error code (HTTP 429 + 'dedicated.corridor.hard_limit')
Autoscaler: emit hints as statsd metrics and a single 'corridor_saturation' gauge aggregated per-pool for the autoscaler to consume
Config: expose corridor params in Dedicated API and Console (read/write restricted to org admins)
